text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today, giving back a small fraction of the sharp 2.7% jump from yesterday. The move is modest noise around a very strong two-week run — the stock is up 11.8% since early October, driven mainly by crude oil prices surging from the mid-$90s to nearly $102 per barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and shipping in the Middle East have tightened supply concerns and pushed Brent crude above $109.

Today's pullback likely reflects some profit-taking after that rapid climb, and possibly traders parsing mixed signals: while geopolitical risk to oil supply remains real, yesterday's news about potential diplomatic progress in the Middle East gave some traders reason to book gains. Oil refiner stocks like this one tend to swing on both crude price moves and shifts in how markets price the risk of further disruptions.
